title: First-principles insights into interfacial electronic, optical and photocatalytic water splitting in HfN 2 /Sc 2 CF 2  van der Waals heterostructure
content: The rational construction of two-dimensional (2D) van der Waals (vdW) heterostructures provides an effective approach for tailoring interfacial electronic and optical properties toward solar-driven water splitting. In this work, we systematically investigate the HfN2/Sc2CF2 vdW heterostructure using first-principles calculations. The HfN2/Sc2CF2 vdW heterostructure exhibits an indirect band gap and type-II band alignment, together with favorable structural, dynamical, and thermal stability at room temperature. Interfacial charge redistribution, accompanied by an electrostatic potential difference, establishes an intrinsic interfacial dipole and built-in electric field, leading to a pronounced reconstruction of the band-edge positions. The resulting band alignment supports a Z-scheme charge-transfer mechanism that preserves sufficient redox driving forces for overall water splitting. Moreover, the HfN2/Sc2CF2 heterostructure exhibits enhanced optical absorption, with a maximum absorption coefficient of 1.92 × 105 cm−1 in the visible-light region, and achieves a high solar-to-hydrogen (STH) conversion efficiency of 14.79%. These results demonstrate that the HfN2/Sc2CF2 heterostructure possesses suitable structural, electronic, optical, and photocatalytic characteristics for potential applications in solar-driven overall water splitting.
